newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegroairlines buys first plane - news agency.
newsitem.headline: Montenegroairlines buys first plane - news agency.

text.p: Montenegroairlines, the first air carrier in the Yugoslav republic of Montenegro, has formally begun to operate after obtaining its first aircraft, the state news agency Tanjug reported on Tuesday.
"Montenegroairlines has purchased a 75-seat Fokker-28 for $3 million from the Belgian comany TAT," director of the fledgling air carrier Dragan Popovic was quoted by Tanjug as saying.
The plane, which is 14 years old, will initially fly passengers on commercial charter flights.
The first test flight will be carried out in about 10 days, and the first commercial flight is expected in 60 days at the latest, Tanjug said.
Later, when Montenegroairlines gets permission to join regular air traffic, regular domestic and international flights will begin, the report said.
The first planned domestic destination will be between Belgrade and the Montenegrin capital Podgorica.
The air carrier plans to obtain another similar aircraft in France by the end of the year, Tanjug said.
Montenegroairlines was formed in late 1994 with majority state capital and founding investments by 34 biggest Montenegrin companies.
